channel.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
channel.description: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

item.title: Trump's messaging meanders as GOP makes final push toward Election Day
item.description: President Trump crisscrosses the country with scattershot closing messages ahead of the midterm elections.

item.title: Larry Sabato on Trump's messaging and the issues driving voters to the polls
item.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with political analyst Larry Sabato about President Trump's messaging and the issues likely to determine the outcome of the midterm elections.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with political analyst Larry Sabato about President Trump's messaging and the issues likely to determine the outcome of the midterm elections.

item.title: Tampa Bay Rays extends World Series against the Milwaukee Brewers
item.description: The Tampa Bay Rays won a thrilling 12-inning game to keep their World Series hopes alive. The Milwaukee Brewers have a 3-1 lead as the Series goes to Game 5.
item.content:encoded: The Tampa Bay Rays won a thrilling 12-inning game to keep their World Series hopes alive. The Milwaukee Brewers have a 3-1 lead as the Series goes to Game 5.

item.title: New teachers union president wants to steer educators away from partisan politics
item.description: NEA President Princess Moss wants to move her organization, the nation's largest labor union, toward issue-based advocacy — and away from party politics.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Iran war and cost-of-living take center stage in Virginia congressional race
item.description: High prices and long deployments are shaping this year's race in Virginia's Second Congressional District. The area with deep Navy ties has been a kind of political bellwether.

item.title: Partial results from Israel's contentious election show no clear winner
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc was leading opposition rival Gadi Eisenkot. Arab parties had a strong showing, and a key question now is whether Eisenkot's bloc will consider forming a coalition with them.
item.content:encoded:
